title: From 100% coverage to real confidence
prompt:
The starter test runs every line of `computeBalances` (and `splitEvenly`), so a coverage report would show 100%. Yet it checks only that three names come back.

Strengthen the suite until it catches three hidden bugs that the 100% suite misses: one **debits** the payer instead of crediting them, one **floors** each share so leftover cents disappear (balances no longer add up to zero), and one **overwrites** the payer's balance instead of adding to it when they pay twice. The rules are in the subject's comment.
hints: Replace the key-count assertion with the exact result: Ana pays 3000 split three ways, so `{ Ana: 2000, Ben: -1000, Cai: -1000 }`.
Use a bill that does not divide evenly, such as 1000 between three people, and assert that the balances add up to 0.
Give the same payer two expenses and check that both are counted.
explanation: Coverage stayed at 100% the whole time: your new tests ran no line the old one didn't. What changed is **what the tests check**. The exact `toEqual` on the first expense catches the sign error. A bill of 1000 cents between three people leaves a cent over, so floored shares make the balances add up to +1 instead of 0; the sum invariant from section 2 catches it. Two expenses from the same payer exercise accumulation, which a single expense never can, even though the accumulating line was already 'covered'. That's the gap between execution and verification, and it's what mutation testing measures directly.

checks.passes: All your tests pass against the real computeBalances
checks.catches-payer-debited: Catches the version that debits the payer
checks.catches-floored-shares: Catches the version that loses leftover cents
checks.catches-overwrites-payer: Catches the version that overwrites the payer's balance
